text.content: During a pilot session, a consultant asked the agent to check the engagement status for a specific client project. The agent retrieved a chunk from the Operations Handbook about project classification tiers, technically related, but not what the consultant needed. The consultant needed live engagement data, not policy documentation.

text.content: The problem is that the agent is currently a single path where every query goes to the Agent Node, which then decides what to do. As the agent gains more capabilities, that single-path architecture becomes a bottleneck. Queries that need live data compete with queries that need document retrieval, and the agent has to reason its way to the right tool every time.

rich_text.plain_text: The problem is that the agent is currently a single path where every query goes to the Agent Node, which then decides what to do. As the agent gains more capabilities, that single-path architecture becomes a bottleneck. Queries that need live data compete with queries that need document retrieval, and the agent has to reason its way to the right tool every time.

text.content: Conditional routing solves this by making some decisions explicit and deterministic. Instead of asking the agent to figure out whether a query needs live data or knowledge retrieval, the Condition Node evaluates a rule and routes the query before the agent even sees it.

text.content: The Condition Node routes the workflow based on a fixed rule. It compares input values using logical operators like equals, contains, greater than, or is empty. If the rule evaluates to true, execution continues down the true branch; if false, down the false branch.

text.content: The Condition Node is a precise, fast, and reliable routing mechanism when the routing logic is unambiguous. Keyword-based rules work well when trigger phrases are distinct and do not appear in other contexts. When the same word or phrase can mean different things depending on context, deterministic routing produces incorrect results that are silent and hard to detect.
